transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Ana (CSM), Lena Ortiz (Apollo Head of Platform), Markus Lee (ML Eng), Sasha Bennett (CTO), Tom Rivers (Infra)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm jordan from redwood, i'm the AE on this account, with priya our solutions eng and ana from customer success. how's everyone doing?
[00:10] Lena: good, thanks. quick background — we're apollo systems, ecommerce orchestration, dealing with chat + search assistants across web and merchant dashboards. evaluating options for inference: hosted first but need dedicated/private for payments/regulatory flows.
[00:25] Jordan: great, that's exactly what we hear. today we'd like to understand your integration surface — SDKs, langchain/llamaindex usage, if you plan to run a gateway/proxy, rate limits, observability. any key success criteria or timelines?
[00:40] Sasha: timeline is Q1 pilot, production in Q2 if things look good. success is latency under 300ms p50 for interactive chat and cost below our current baseline for embeddings.
[00:55] Markus: technical detail: we're on k8s in gcp, use envoy as gateway, we have a small LLM infra team. majority of traffic is text-generation for chat, plus batch embeddings for search reindex every 6 hours.
[01:10] Priya: perfect — quick question about your orchestration: will you front Redwood with your existing gateway or use our gateway? we support both hosted API directly or customers put a proxy in front for routing to Dedicated/Private.
[01:25] Tom: we prefer to keep envoy in front for auth and auditing. we want a signed token flow from redwood if hosted, or mutual TLS if dedicated/private.
[01:40] Jordan: absolutely — hosted supports signed bearer tokens; for Dedicated/Private we support mTLS and VPC peering. we also have private control plane option and KMS/HSM integrations for key management.
[01:55] Markus: how do SDKs fit in — does redwood have official python/node sdks? and examples for langchain or llamaindex?
[02:05] Priya: yes, official SDKs for python and node, plus example connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex. we have a starter repo that shows chunking, retriever chains, and how to swap model endpoints between hosted/dedicated with one config. i'll share that link after. (note: transcription may show Redewood or Redwood-Dedicated in older docs)
[02:30] Lena: any gotchas when using LlamaIndex? we currently use it for our product QA.
[02:35] Priya: mostly around streaming responses and tokenization differences — we have adapters for LlamaIndex which handle streaming and partial responses; watch out for llm config differences when you switch quantized models. also KV cache behavior differs for hosted vs dedicated due to shared vs isolated caches.
[03:00] Sasha: can you explain KV cache and batching? we want predictable latency.
[03:05] Priya: sure — our serving runtime does continuous batching with adaptive batch sizes; for Dedicated you get isolated GPU pools and can tune batch windows for latency SLOs. KV cache helps with prefix caching to avoid recomputing past tokens for chat sessions. hosted uses multi-tenant caches but we offer per-customer prefix cache pins for enterprise.
[03:30] Markus: rate limits — how are per-route quotas configured? we need burst control and per-team quotas inside our org.
[03:40] Jordan: we expose rate limits on API keys and support per-route quotas via the console. quotas can be enforced on token usage or request counts, and we have soft/hard limits, burst windows, and webhook notifications when thresholds are crossed. for Dedicated we can map quotas to pools or routes.
[04:05] Tom: observability — what hooks do you provide? we need traces, per-request token breakdown, and latency percentiles exported to prometheus or datadog.
[04:15] Priya: Redwood Console provides per-model route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and tracing hooks. we export metrics via prometheus endpoints and support OTLP for traces; you can tag requests with your correlation IDs and we preserve them through the runtime. we also provide access to raw request/response artifacts in the audit logs (with redaction options).
[04:45] Lena: encryption and compliance — SOC 2, SSO, audit logs, kms?
[04:50] Jordan: yes SOC 2, SAML/SSO, RBAC in the console. for encryption we support customer-managed keys via KMS, HSM options on Private. we'll share the security pack.
[05:05] Markus: about latency — you said p50 300ms target for interactive chat. what about p95?
[05:10] Priya: p95 will depend on model choice and sequence length. for short prompts with optimized kernels and batching we typically see p95 under 700ms on Dedicated; hosted numbers can vary by region and load but we publish perf profiles for each curated model. we can run a benchmark with your payloads.
[06:00] Jordan: any constraints with traffic spikes? we do autoscaling but for predictable SLA-backed throughput you'd want Dedicated reserved capacity or our burst capacity option.
[06:10] Sasha: cost — curious about cost delta between Hosted vs Dedicated.
[06:15] Jordan: Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved monthly commits but lowers unit cost at scale. we'll send a sample TCO calc with your traffic profile — that will show crossover point.
[06:35] Markus: we use LangChain heavily for orchestration, plus a few custom retrievers. will switching models for fallback be smooth? e.g., default to a cheaper quantized variant on overload?
[06:45] Priya: yes, smart routing supports model variants and automated fallback based on policy (latency/cost/region). you can configure rollout policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants if capacity's constrained.
[07:10] Lena: integration effort — how long to integrate SDK and replace our current endpoint?
[07:15] Priya: basic SDK integration for text generation is a few days for an engineer to wire up. using LangChain connectors and retriever wiring is a week to production for a small team, plus testing and policy checks. Private/VPC onboarding takes longer — typically 4–8 weeks depending on network approvals.
[07:40] Tom: about gateway pattern: we'd like envoy to authenticate and rate limit; then forward to redwood. do you support signed JWTs with embedded org claims so we can map quotas?
[07:50] Jordan: yes we support signed JWTs and we can map claims to quota keys. we also support API keys per route and per-team scopes.
[08:10] Markus: anecdotal transcription glitch — earlier you said 'KV cache for per-customer prefix pins' — can you send docs?
[08:16] Priya: yes will attach docs, and i'll include a diagram showing differences between hosted shared cache vs dedicated isolated cache behavior.
[08:30] Sasha: security review — our security team will want to run a deep dive. what's typical for SOC2 plus VPC?
[08:36] Jordan: we do a security questionnaire, provide SOC 2 report, network diagrams, and for Private we do an onboarding call with our infra security team to review peering and access. many customers also request pen tests which we coordinate.
[09:00] Lena: can you talk about observability hooks for function/tool calling? we do lots of tool orchestration and need to trace tool calls.end-to-end.
[09:08] Priya: we pass structured function/tool call metadata through traces and provide tooling to correlate those calls in the console; you can hook into our webhook sink for tool invocation events as well.
[09:30] Markus: does redwood support custom rate-limiting at the model-route level inside the runtime for different teams?
[09:36] Priya: yes — route-level quotas and model-level limits. in Dedicated you can partition pools per-team for strict isolation.
[10:00] (Back-and-forth about specific SDK code)
[10:05] Priya: example python snippet:
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="<key>")
response = client.generate(model="redwood-llama2-13b", prompt="...", stream=True)
// we also provide LangChain adapter: LLMChain(llm=RedwoodLLM(...))
(rough transcription; code in repo)
[12:15] Jordan: ok let's recap and next steps
[12:20] Jordan: priya will run a bench with apollo payloads; i'll send pricing and SOC2/security pack; lena will share traffic percentiles and SLOs; we schedule a 2-hour deep technical session next week with tom and markus.
[12:35] Lena: that works. we also want the example LangChain/LlamaIndex repo and the envoy proxy patterns.
[12:45] Jordan: will do. any final questions?
[12:50] Sasha: only that dedicated onboarding timeline and pilot terms — can you include in the follow-up?
[12:55] Jordan: yes, included. thanks everyone.

(End)
